## File: `test.html`

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">

<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>AP Exam Engine – EduQuest</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="test.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/katex.min.css">
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/katex.min.js"></script>
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/contrib/auto-render.min.js"></script>
  
  <script>
    window.MathJax = {
      tex: {
        inlineMath: [['$', '$'], ['\\(', '\\)']],
        displayMath: [['$$', '$$'], ['\\[', '\\]']],
        processEscapes: true
      },
      options: {
        skipHtmlTags: ['script', 'noscript', 'style', 'textarea', 'pre', 'code']
      }
    };
  </script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" id="MathJax-script" async></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@supabase/supabase-js@2"></script>
  <script src="supabase.js"></script>
  <script src="access-check.js"></script>
  <script src="questions.js"></script>
</head>

<body>

  <!-- HEADER -->
  <header class="test-hdr">
    <div class="test-info">
      <span class="test-title" id="testTitle">AP Calculus Exam</span>
      <span class="test-badge" id="testBadge">Diagnostic</span>
    </div>
    <div class="timer-box" id="timerBox">
      <span>⏱️</span>
      <span id="timerDisplay">45:00</span>
    </div>
    <div style="display:flex; gap:10px;">
      <a href="index.html" class="btn-nav" style="text-decoration:none;">🏠 Homepage</a>
      <button class="btn-nav" onclick="togglePalette()">📋 Palette</button>
      <button class="btn-nav btn-submit" onclick="confirmSubmit()">Submit Test</button>
    </div>
  </header>

  <!-- BODY CONTENT -->
  <div class="test-body">
    <div class="question-area">
      <div class="q-meta-row">
        <div class="q-number" id="qNumber">Question 1 of 30</div>
        <div class="q-tags">
          <span class="tag" id="qTopicTag">Limits</span>
          <span class="tag medium" id="qDiffTag">Medium</span>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Question Text -->
      <div class="q-text" id="qText">Loading question content...</div>

      <!-- MCQ Options -->
      <div class="options-list" id="optionsList"></div>

      <!-- FRQ Input Box -->
      <div class="frq-box" id="frqBox" style="display:none;">
        <label style="display:block; font-size:0.85rem; font-weight:700; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.6); margin-bottom:8px;">FREE RESPONSE SOLUTION</label>
        <textarea id="frqTextarea" class="frq-textarea" placeholder="Type your step-by-step mathematical work, justification, or final numerical answer here..."></textarea>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- BOTTOM FOOTER NAVIGATION -->
  <footer class="test-ftr">
    <button class="btn-nav" id="btnPrev" onclick="navQuestion(-1)">← Previous</button>
    <button class="btn-nav" id="btnFlag" onclick="toggleFlag()">🚩 Flag for Review</button>
    <button class="btn-nav btn-primary" id="btnNext" onclick="navQuestion(1)">Next Question →</button>
  </footer>

  <!-- PALETTE DRAWER -->
  <div class="palette-modal" id="paletteDrawer">
    <h3 style="font-family:'Syne',sans-serif; font-size:1.1rem; margin-bottom:12px;">Question Navigator</h3>
    <div class="palette-grid" id="paletteGrid"></div>
  </div>

  <script>
    let testId = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('id') || 'ap-diag-1';
    let currentTest = null;
    let questions = [];
    let currentIndex = 0;
    let userAnswers = {};
    let flaggedList = new Set();
    let timeRemaining = 45 * 60;
    let timerInterval = null;
    let studentInfo = { name: 'Student', email: 'student@example.com', phone: '' };

    const SESSION_KEY = `eduquest_ap_session_${testId}`;
    let examEndTime = null;

    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', async () => {
      // Load current test configuration
      currentTest = AP_TEST_DATA[testId] || AP_TEST_DATA['ap-diag-1'];
      questions = currentTest.questions || [];
      const durationSeconds = (currentTest.timeLimitMinutes || 45) * 60;

      // Secure timestamp-based session persistence
      let sessionData = null;
      try {
        const raw = localStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY);
        if (raw) sessionData = JSON.parse(raw);
      } catch (e) { }

      const now = Date.now();
      if (sessionData && sessionData.endTime && sessionData.startTime) {
        // Tamper guard: prevent extending endTime beyond configured test duration
        const maxAllowedEnd = sessionData.startTime + (durationSeconds * 1000) + 5000;
        if (sessionData.endTime > maxAllowedEnd) {
          sessionData.endTime = maxAllowedEnd;
        }
        examEndTime = sessionData.endTime;
        timeRemaining = Math.max(0, Math.floor((examEndTime - now) / 1000));
      } else {
        const startTime = now;
        examEndTime = startTime + (durationSeconds * 1000);
        timeRemaining = durationSeconds;
        localStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, JSON.stringify({
          startTime,
          endTime: examEndTime,
          durationSeconds
        }));
      }

      document.getElementById('testTitle').textContent = currentTest.title;
      document.getElementById('testBadge').textContent = currentTest.testType || 'AP Prep';

      // Load logged in student info
      const client = window.supabase.createClient(SUPABASE_CONFIG.url, SUPABASE_CONFIG.anonKey);
      const { data: { session } } = await client.auth.getSession();
      if (session && session.user) {
        studentInfo.email = session.user.email;
        studentInfo.name = session.user.user_metadata?.full_name || session.user.email.split('@')[0];
        studentInfo.phone = session.user.user_metadata?.phone || '';
      }

      // Save registration log to ap_user
      saveRegistration(studentInfo, currentTest.title);

      if (timeRemaining <= 0) {
        alert('⏰ Test time limit has expired! Submitting test automatically.');
        submitTest();
        return;
      }

      startTimer();
      renderQuestion();
      renderPalette();
    });

    function startTimer() {
      function updateClock() {
        const now = Date.now();
        timeRemaining = Math.max(0, Math.floor((examEndTime - now) / 1000));

        if (timeRemaining <= 0) {
          clearInterval(timerInterval);
          localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY);
          alert('⏰ Time limit reached! Submitting test automatically.');
          submitTest();
          return;
        }

        const mins = Math.floor(timeRemaining / 60);
        const secs = timeRemaining % 60;
        const display = `${mins.toString().padStart(2, '0')}:${secs.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`;
        const el = document.getElementById('timerDisplay');
        if (el) el.textContent = display;

        if (timeRemaining < 300) { // < 5 mins
          document.getElementById('timerBox')?.classList.add('warning');
        }
      }

      updateClock();
      timerInterval = setInterval(updateClock, 1000);
    }

    function renderQuestion() {
      if (questions.length === 0) return;
      const q = questions[currentIndex];

      document.getElementById('qNumber').textContent = `Question ${currentIndex + 1} of ${questions.length}`;
      document.getElementById('qTopicTag').textContent = q.topic || 'AP Calculus';
      
      const diffEl = document.getElementById('qDiffTag');
      diffEl.textContent = (q.difficulty || 'medium').toUpperCase();
      diffEl.className = `tag ${q.difficulty || 'medium'}`;

      document.getElementById('qText').innerHTML = q.question;

      const optsContainer = document.getElementById('optionsList');
      const frqContainer = document.getElementById('frqBox');

      if (q.isFRQ) {
        optsContainer.style.display = 'none';
        frqContainer.style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('frqTextarea').value = userAnswers[q.id] || '';
      } else {
        frqContainer.style.display = 'none';
        optsContainer.style.display = 'flex';
        optsContainer.innerHTML = '';

        const prefixes = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'];
        (q.options || []).forEach((optText, idx) => {
          const pref = prefixes[idx] || `${idx+1}`;
          const isSelected = userAnswers[q.id] === pref;

          const optCard = document.createElement('div');
          optCard.className = `opt-card ${isSelected ? 'selected' : ''}`;
          optCard.onclick = () => selectOption(q.id, pref);
          optCard.innerHTML = `
            <div class="opt-prefix">${pref}</div>
            <div class="opt-content">${optText}</div>`;
          optsContainer.appendChild(optCard);
        });
      }

      // Typeset math expressions with KaTeX and MathJax
      if (window.renderMathInElement) {
        renderMathInElement(document.querySelector('.question-area') || document.body, {
          delimiters: [
            {left: '$$', right: '$$', display: true},
            {left: '$', right: '$', display: false},
            {left: '\\(', right: '\\)', display: false},
            {left: '\\[', right: '\\]', display: true}
          ],
          throwOnError: false
        });
      }
      if (window.MathJax && MathJax.typesetPromise) {
        if (MathJax.typesetClear) MathJax.typesetClear();
        MathJax.typesetPromise([document.querySelector('.question-area') || document.body]).catch(() => {});
      }

      document.getElementById('btnPrev').style.visibility = currentIndex === 0 ? 'hidden' : 'visible';
      document.getElementById('btnNext').textContent = currentIndex === questions.length - 1 ? 'Review & Submit' : 'Next Question →';
      renderPalette();
    }

    function selectOption(qId, pref) {
      userAnswers[qId] = pref;
      renderQuestion();
    }

    // Save FRQ input on change
    document.getElementById('frqTextarea').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
      const q = questions[currentIndex];
      if (q && q.isFRQ) {
        userAnswers[q.id] = e.target.value;
        renderPalette();
      }
    });

    function navQuestion(dir) {
      const newIdx = currentIndex + dir;
      if (newIdx >= 0 && newIdx < questions.length) {
        currentIndex = newIdx;
        renderQuestion();
      } else if (newIdx === questions.length) {
        confirmSubmit();
      }
    }

    function toggleFlag() {
      const qId = questions[currentIndex].id;
      if (flaggedList.has(qId)) flaggedList.delete(qId);
      else flaggedList.add(qId);
      renderPalette();
    }

    function togglePalette() {
      document.getElementById('paletteDrawer').classList.toggle('open');
    }

    function renderPalette() {
      const grid = document.getElementById('paletteGrid');
      grid.innerHTML = '';

      questions.forEach((q, idx) => {
        const item = document.createElement('div');
        let statusClass = '';
        if (userAnswers[q.id]) statusClass = 'answered';
        if (flaggedList.has(q.id)) statusClass = 'flagged';
        if (idx === currentIndex) statusClass += ' active';

        item.className = `palette-item ${statusClass}`;
        item.textContent = idx + 1;
        item.onclick = () => {
          currentIndex = idx;
          renderQuestion();
          document.getElementById('paletteDrawer').classList.remove('open');
        };
        grid.appendChild(item);
      });
    }

    function confirmSubmit() {
      const answeredCount = Object.keys(userAnswers).length;
      const total = questions.length;
      if (confirm(`Are you sure you want to submit your test?\n\nAnswered: ${answeredCount} / ${total}`)) {
        submitTest();
      }
    }

    async function submitTest() {
      clearInterval(timerInterval);
      localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY);
      localStorage.removeItem(`eduquest_ap_time_${testId}`);

      let correct = 0;
      let wrong = 0;
      let unattempted = 0;
      let frqCount = 0;
      const details = [];

      questions.forEach(q => {
        const chosen = userAnswers[q.id];
        let status = 'unattempted';

        if (!chosen || chosen.toString().trim() === '') {
          unattempted++;
        } else if (q.isFRQ) {
          status = 'frq_submitted';
          frqCount++;
          // FRQs are student-written work evaluated against rubrics; not auto-scored as MCQ correct
        } else if (chosen === q.answer) {
          correct++;
          status = 'correct';
        } else {
          wrong++;
          status = 'wrong';
        }

        details.push({
          id: q.id,
          topic: q.topic || 'General',
          difficulty: q.difficulty || 'medium',
          status: status,
          isFRQ: !!q.isFRQ,
          chosen: chosen || 'Unattempted',
          answer: q.answer,
          question: q.question,
          options: q.options || [],
          explanation: q.explanation || q.rubric || ''
        });
      });

      const mcqQuestions = questions.filter(q => !q.isFRQ);
      const mcqTotal = mcqQuestions.length;
      const total = questions.length;
      const pct = mcqTotal > 0 ? Math.round((correct / mcqTotal) * 100) : 100;
      const apScore = calculateAPScore(pct);

      const result = {
        student: studentInfo,
        examName: currentTest.title,
        testType: currentTest.testType || 'AP Test',
        topicNumber: 1,
        correct,
        wrong,
        unattempted,
        total,
        pct,
        ap_score: apScore,
        submitTime: new Date().toISOString(),
        answers: userAnswers,
        details: details
      };

      // Store in localStorage for instant report view
      localStorage.setItem('eduquest_ap_last_report', JSON.stringify(result));

      // Save to Supabase ap_reports table
      await saveToSupabase(result);

      // Redirect to full report page
      window.location.href = 'report.html';
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">

<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>AP Score Report – EduQuest</title>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Syne:wght@600;700;800&family=IBM+Plex+Sans:wght@300;400;500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="index.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/katex.min.css">
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/katex.min.js"></script>
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.8/dist/contrib/auto-render.min.js"></script>
  <script>
    window.MathJax = {
      tex: {
        inlineMath: [['$', '$'], ['\\(', '\\)']],
        displayMath: [['$$', '$$'], ['\\[', '\\]']],
        processEscapes: true
      }
    };
  </script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" id="MathJax-script" async></script>
  <style>
    body { background: #0a0a10; color: #fff; padding-bottom: 60px; }
    
    .report-card {
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
      border-radius: 20px;
      padding: 36px;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .report-hdr {
      text-align: center;
      margin-bottom: 28px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
      padding-bottom: 20px;
    }

    .score-hero-box {
      background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.2), rgba(79, 70, 229, 0.1));
      border: 1px solid rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.4);
      border-radius: 20px;
      padding: 28px;
      text-align: center;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .big-score {
      font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif;
      font-size: 3rem;
      font-weight: 800;
      color: #fff;
    }

    .pct-val {
      font-size: 1.4rem;
      color: #c084fc;
      font-weight: 700;
      margin-bottom: 14px;
    }

    .ap-badge {
      display: inline-block;
      background: #7c3aed;
      color: #fff;
      font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif;
      font-size: 1.25rem;
      font-weight: 800;
      padding: 8px 20px;
      border-radius: 30px;
      box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.5);
    }

    .metrics-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
      gap: 14px;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .metric-card {
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 16px;
      text-align: center;
    }

    .metric-val {
      font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif;
      font-size: 1.5rem;
      font-weight: 700;
    }

    .metric-lbl {
      font-size: 0.76rem;
      color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5);
      text-transform: uppercase;
      margin-top: 4px;
    }

    /* ── BAR PROGRESS ROWS ───────────────────────────────────── */
    .section-title {
      font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif;
      font-size: 1.25rem;
      font-weight: 800;
      margin-bottom: 16px;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
    }

    .bar-row {
      margin-bottom: 16px;
    }

    .bar-label-line {
      display: flex;
      justify-content: space-between;
      font-size: 0.9rem;
      font-weight: 600;
      margin-bottom: 6px;
    }

    .bar-track {
      height: 12px;
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
      border-radius: 10px;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .bar-fill {
      height: 100%;
      background: linear-gradient(90deg, #7c3aed, #60a5fa);
      border-radius: 10px;
      transition: width 0.6s ease;
    }

    .strengths-box {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
      gap: 20px;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .strength-card {
      background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.08);
      border: 1px solid rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.25);
      border-radius: 14px;
      padding: 20px;
    }

    .improve-card {
      background: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.08);
      border: 1px solid rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.25);
      border-radius: 14px;
      padding: 20px;
    }

    .bullet-list {
      list-style: none;
      margin-top: 10px;
    }

    .bullet-list li {
      font-size: 0.9rem;
      margin-bottom: 8px;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
    }

    /* ── QUESTION REVIEW & OPTIONS ─────────────────────────── */
    .q-review-item {
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 20px;
      margin-bottom: 18px;
    }

    .q-review-item.correct { border-left: 5px solid #10b981; }
    .q-review-item.wrong { border-left: 5px solid #ef4444; }
    .q-review-item.unattempted { border-left: 5px solid #6b7280; }

    .report-options-grid {
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      gap: 8px;
      margin: 14px 0;
    }

    .report-opt-item {
      display: flex;
      align-items: flex-start;
      gap: 12px;
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07);
      border-radius: 8px;
      padding: 10px 14px;
      font-size: 0.9rem;
      line-height: 1.4;
    }

    .report-opt-pref {
      font-weight: 700;
      width: 26px;
      height: 26px;
      border-radius: 6px;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      font-size: 0.8rem;
      flex-shrink: 0;
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
      color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8);
    }

    .report-opt-item.is-correct {
      background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.08);
      border-color: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.35);
    }
    .report-opt-item.is-correct .report-opt-pref {
      background: #10b981;
      color: #fff;
    }

    .report-opt-item.is-user-wrong {
      background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.08);
      border-color: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.35);
    }
    .report-opt-item.is-user-wrong .report-opt-pref {
      background: #ef4444;
      color: #fff;
    }

    .opt-badge-tag {
      margin-left: auto;
      font-size: 0.75rem;
      font-weight: 700;
      padding: 2px 8px;
      border-radius: 4px;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    }
    .badge-correct { background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.2); color: #34d399; }
    .badge-wrong { background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.2); color: #f87171; }

    @media print {
      body { background: #fff !important; color: #111827 !important; padding: 0 !important; }
      .hdr, .print-btn-row { display: none !important; }
      .wrap { max-width: 100% !important; margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important; }
      .report-card, .metric-card, .score-hero-box, .q-review-item, .strength-card, .improve-card {
        border: 1px solid #e5e7eb !important;
        background: #ffffff !important;
        color: #111827 !important;
        box-shadow: none !important;
        page-break-inside: avoid;
        break-inside: avoid;
      }
      .big-score, .ap-badge, .metric-val, .section-title, h1, h2, h3 { color: #111827 !important; }
      .score-hero-box { border: 2px solid #7c3aed !important; }
      .ap-badge { background: #7c3aed !important; color: #fff !important; }
      .q-review-item.correct { border-left: 6px solid #10b981 !important; }
      .q-review-item.wrong { border-left: 6px solid #ef4444 !important; }
      .q-review-item.unattempted { border-left: 6px solid #6b7280 !important; }
      .report-opt-item { border: 1px solid #e5e7eb !important; background: #f9fafb !important; color: #111827 !important; }
      .report-opt-item.is-correct { border-color: #10b981 !important; background: #ecfdf5 !important; }
      .report-opt-item.is-user-wrong { border-color: #ef4444 !important; background: #fef2f2 !important; }
      .report-opt-pref { color: #000 !important; }
    }
  </style>
</head>

<body>

  <header class="hdr">
    <a href="index.html" class="brand">
      <span>EduQuest</span>
      <span class="brand-pill">AP Report</span>
    </a>
    <div class="hdr-right print-btn-row">
      <button onclick="window.print()" class="hdr-btn" style="background:#7c3aed; color:#fff; border:none;">🖨️ Print / Save PDF</button>
      <a href="dashboard.html" class="hdr-btn">📊 Dashboard</a>
      <a href="index.html" class="hdr-btn">🏠 Homepage / Portal</a>
    </div>
  </header>

  <div class="wrap" style="max-width:900px;">
    
    <div class="report-card" id="reportContent">
      
      <div class="report-hdr">
        <h1 style="font-family:'Syne',sans-serif; font-size:1.8rem; margin-bottom:4px;" id="rStudentName">Student Score Report</h1>
        <p style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5); font-size:0.9rem;" id="rExamTitle">AP Calculus Diagnostic Test</p>
        <p style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.35); font-size:0.78rem; margin-top:4px;" id="rSubmitTime"></p>
      </div>

'<span style="color:#f87171; font-weight:700;">✕ Incorrect</span>' : (d.status === 'frq_submitted' ? '<span style="color:#60a5fa; font-weight:700;">📝 FRQ Submitted</span>' : '<span style="color:#9ca3af; font-weight:700;">— Unattempted</span>'));

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

// Load main questions.js
const questionsJsContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'questions.js'), 'utf8');

// Evaluate AP_TEST_DATA from questions.js
const vm = require('vm');
const sandbox = { console };
vm.createContext(sandbox);
vm.runInContext(questionsJsContent.replace('const AP_TEST_DATA', 'this.AP_TEST_DATA'), sandbox);

const AP_TEST_DATA = sandbox.AP_TEST_DATA;
const indexHtmlContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'index.html'), 'utf8');
const testToSubjectMap = {};

const match = indexHtmlContent.match(/const SUBJECT_TEST_CARDS = (\{[\s\S]*?\n    \};)/);
if (match) {
    try {
        const rawObjStr = match[1].replace(/;\s*$/, '');
        const subjectCardsObj = vm.runInContext(`(${rawObjStr})`, sandbox);
        Object.keys(subjectCardsObj).forEach(subId => {
            (subjectCardsObj[subId] || []).forEach(card => {
                testToSubjectMap[card.id] = subId;
            });
        });
    } catch(e) {
        console.error("Warning: could not parse SUBJECT_TEST_CARDS from index.html", e);
    }
}

function getSubjectIdForTest(testId) {
    if (testToSubjectMap[testId]) return testToSubjectMap[testId];
    if (testId === 'ap-diag-1') return 'ap-calc-ab';
    if (testId.includes('calcbc') || testId.includes('calc-bc')) return 'ap-calc-bc';
    if (testId.includes('calc')) return 'ap-calc-ab';
    if (testId.includes('csa')) return 'ap-cs-a';
    if (testId.includes('csp')) return 'ap-csp';
    if (testId.includes('precalc')) return 'ap-precalc';
    if (testId.includes('stats')) return 'ap-stats';
    if (testId.includes('bio')) return 'ap-bio';
    if (testId.includes('chem')) return 'ap-chem';
    if (testId.includes('env')) return 'ap-env';
    if (testId.includes('phys1')) return 'ap-phys-1';
    if (testId.includes('phys2')) return 'ap-phys-2';
    if (testId.includes('physc-mech') || ['kinematics', 'forces', 'momentum', 'energy', 'gravitation', 'rotation', 'shm', 'tension', 'inclines', 'graphs'].some(t => testId.includes(t) && testId.includes('physc'))) return 'ap-phys-c-mech';
    if (testId.includes('physc-em') || ['electrostatics', 'circuits', 'magnetism', 'induction', 'fields', 'gauss', 'capacitors', 'inductors'].some(t => testId.includes(t) && testId.includes('physc'))) return 'ap-phys-c-em';
    if (testId.includes('englang')) return 'ap-eng-lang';
    if (testId.includes('englit')) return 'ap-eng-lit';
    if (testId.includes('ush')) return 'ap-ush';
    if (testId.includes('world')) return 'ap-world';
    if (testId.includes('euro')) return 'ap-euro';
    if (testId.includes('macro')) return 'ap-macro';
    if (testId.includes('micro')) return 'ap-micro';
    if (testId.includes('psych')) return 'ap-psych';
    if (testId.includes('usgov')) return 'ap-usgov';
    if (testId.includes('compgov')) return 'ap-compgov';
    if (testId.includes('humgeo')) return 'ap-humgeo';
    if (testId.includes('afam')) return 'ap-afam';
    if (testId.includes('arthist')) return 'ap-art-hist';
    if (testId.includes('music')) return 'ap-music';
    if (testId.includes('2dart')) return 'ap-2d-art';
    if (testId.includes('3dart')) return 'ap-3d-art';
    if (testId.includes('drawing')) return 'ap-drawing';
    if (testId.includes('spanishlit')) return 'ap-spanish-lit';
    if (testId.includes('spanish')) return 'ap-spanish-lang';
    if (testId.includes('french')) return 'ap-french';
    if (testId.includes('german')) return 'ap-german';
    if (testId.includes('chinese')) return 'ap-chinese';
    if (testId.includes('japanese')) return 'ap-japanese';
    if (testId.includes('italian')) return 'ap-italian';
    if (testId.includes('latin')) return 'ap-latin';
    if (testId.includes('seminar')) return 'ap-seminar';
    if (testId.includes('research')) return 'ap-research';
    return 'general';
}

const testIds = Object.keys(AP_TEST_DATA);

console.log(`Found ${testIds.length} tests to organize into category folders:`, testIds);

const baseTestsDir = path.join(__dirname, 'tests');

// Clean previous directory structure if needed
if (fs.existsSync(baseTestsDir)) {
    fs.rmSync(baseTestsDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
fs.mkdirSync(baseTestsDir, { recursive: true });

testIds.forEach(testId => {

          .replace(/src='\\/images\\//g, "src='${relRoot}images/");
      }

      document.getElementById('qText').innerHTML = fixImgPaths(q.question || '');

      const optsContainer = document.getElementById('optionsList');
      const frqContainer = document.getElementById('frqBox');

      if (q.isFRQ) {
        optsContainer.style.display = 'none';
        frqContainer.style.display = 'block';
        document.getElementById('frqTextarea').value = userAnswers[q.id] || '';
      } else {
        frqContainer.style.display = 'none';
        optsContainer.style.display = 'flex';
        optsContainer.innerHTML = '';

        const prefixes = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'];
        (q.options || []).forEach((optText, idx) => {
          const pref = prefixes[idx] || \`\${idx+1}\`;
          const isSelected = userAnswers[q.id] === pref;
          
          // Fix paths and strip outer <p> tags from option content
          let renderedOpt = fixImgPaths(optText || '');
          renderedOpt = renderedOpt.replace(/^<p>([\\s\\S]*)<\\/p>$/i, '$1').trim();

          const optCard = document.createElement('div');
          optCard.className = \`opt-card \${isSelected ? 'selected' : ''}\`;
          optCard.onclick = () => selectOption(q.id, pref);
          optCard.innerHTML = \`
            <div class="opt-prefix">\${pref}</div>
            <div class="opt-content">\${renderedOpt || '&nbsp;'}</div>\`;
          optsContainer.appendChild(optCard);
        });
      }

      // Typeset math using KaTeX and/or MathJax
      if (window.renderMathInElement) {
        renderMathInElement(document.querySelector('.question-area') || document.body, {
          delimiters: [
            {left: '$$', right: '$$', display: true},
            {left: '$', right: '$', display: false},
            {left: '\\\\(', right: '\\\\)', display: false},
            {left: '\\\\[', right: '\\\\]', display: true}
          ],
          throwOnError: false
        });
      }
      if (window.MathJax && MathJax.typesetPromise) {
        if (MathJax.typesetClear) MathJax.typesetClear();
        MathJax.typesetPromise([document.querySelector('.question-area') || document.body]).catch(() => {});
      }

      const btnPrev = document.getElementById('btnPrev');
      const btnNext = document.getElementById('btnNext');
      btnPrev.style.visibility = currentIndex === 0 ? 'hidden' : 'visible';
      btnNext.textContent = currentIndex === questions.length - 1 ? 'Review & Submit' : 'Next Question →';
      renderPalette();
    }

    function selectOption(qId, pref) {
      userAnswers[qId] = pref;
      renderQuestion();
    }

    document.getElementById('frqTextarea').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
      const q = questions[currentIndex];
      if (q && q.isFRQ) {
        userAnswers[q.id] = e.target.value;
        renderPalette();
      }
    });

    function navQuestion(dir) {
      const newIdx = currentIndex + dir;
      if (newIdx >= 0 && newIdx < questions.length) {
        currentIndex = newIdx;
        renderQuestion();
      } else if (newIdx === questions.length) {
        confirmSubmit();
      }
    }

    function toggleFlag() {
      const qId = questions[currentIndex].id;
      if (flaggedList.has(qId)) flaggedList.delete(qId);
      else flaggedList.add(qId);
      renderPalette();
    }

    function togglePalette() {
      document.getElementById('paletteDrawer').classList.toggle('open');
    }

    function renderPalette() {
      const grid = document.getElementById('paletteGrid');
      grid.innerHTML = '';

      questions.forEach((q, idx) => {
        const item = document.createElement('div');
        let statusClass = '';
        if (userAnswers[q.id]) statusClass = 'answered';
        if (flaggedList.has(q.id)) statusClass = 'flagged';
        if (idx === currentIndex) statusClass += ' active';

        item.className = \`palette-item \${statusClass}\`;
        item.textContent = idx + 1;
        item.onclick = () => {
          currentIndex = idx;
          renderQuestion();
          document.getElementById('paletteDrawer').classList.remove('open');
        };
        grid.appendChild(item);
      });
    }

    function confirmSubmit() {
      const answeredCount = Object.keys(userAnswers).length;
      const total = questions.length;
      if (confirm(\`Are you sure you want to submit your test?\\n\\nAnswered: \${answeredCount} / \${total}\`)) {
        submitTest();
      }
    }

    async function submitTest() {
      clearInterval(timerInterval);
      localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY);
      localStorage.removeItem(\`eduquest_ap_time_\${testId}\`);

      let correct = 0;
      let wrong = 0;
      let unattempted = 0;
      let frqCount = 0;
      const details = [];

      questions.forEach(q => {
        const chosen = userAnswers[q.id];
        let status = 'unattempted';

        if (!chosen || chosen.toString().trim() === '') {
          unattempted++;
        } else if (q.isFRQ) {
          status = 'frq_submitted';
          frqCount++;
          // FRQs are student-written work evaluated against rubrics; not auto-scored as MCQ correct
        } else if (chosen === q.answer) {
          correct++;
          status = 'correct';
        } else {
          wrong++;
          status = 'wrong';
        }

        details.push({
          id: q.id,
          topic: q.topic || 'General',
          difficulty: q.difficulty || 'medium',
          status: status,
          isFRQ: !!q.isFRQ,
          chosen: chosen || 'Unattempted',
          answer: q.answer,
          question: q.question,
          options: q.options || [],
          explanation: q.explanation || q.rubric || ''
        });
      });

      const mcqQuestions = questions.filter(q => !q.isFRQ);
      const mcqTotal = mcqQuestions.length;
      const total = questions.length;
      const pct = mcqTotal > 0 ? Math.round((correct / mcqTotal) * 100) : 100;
      const apScore = calculateAPScore(pct);

      const result = {
        student: studentInfo,
        examName: currentTest.title,
        testType: currentTest.testType || 'AP Test',
        topicNumber: 1,
        correct,
        wrong,
        unattempted,
        total,
        pct,
        ap_score: apScore,
        submitTime: new Date().toISOString(),
        answers: userAnswers,
        details: details
      };

      localStorage.setItem('eduquest_ap_last_report', JSON.stringify(result));
      await saveToSupabase(result);
      window.location.href = '${relRoot}report.html';
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>`;

    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(testFolder, 'test.html'), htmlContent, 'utf8');
    const relPath = path.relative(__dirname, testFolder).replace(/\\/g, '/');
    console.log(`Created folder: ${relPath} with test.html and questions.js`);
});

console.log('✅ Successfully generated categorized test folders!');

## File: `verify_repaired_questions.js`

```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const vm = require('vm');

const questionsJsContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'questions.js'), 'utf8');
const sandbox = {};
vm.createContext(sandbox);
vm.runInContext(questionsJsContent.replace('const AP_TEST_DATA', 'this.AP_TEST_DATA'), sandbox);
const AP_TEST_DATA = sandbox.AP_TEST_DATA;

const qaLog = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'qa_remediation_log.json'), 'utf8'));

console.log(`Auditing ${qaLog.length} repaired questions against independent solutions...`);

const report = [];
let passCount = 0;
let failCount = 0;

qaLog.forEach(entry => {
  const test = AP_TEST_DATA[entry.testId];
  if (!test) {
    report.push({
      testId: entry.testId,
      questionId: entry.questionId,
      independentAnswer: "N/A",
      storedAnswer: "MISSING_TEST",
      answerMatch: false,
      explanationStatus: "FAIL",
      questionValidity: "FAIL",
      intentStatus: "FAIL",
      severity: "CRITICAL"
    });
    failCount++;
    return;
  }

  const q = test.questions.find(x => x.id === entry.questionId);
  if (!q) {
    report.push({
      testId: entry.testId,
      questionId: entry.questionId,
      independentAnswer: "N/A",
      storedAnswer: "MISSING_QUESTION",
      answerMatch: false,
      explanationStatus: "FAIL",
      questionValidity: "FAIL",
      intentStatus: "FAIL",
      severity: "CRITICAL"
    });
    failCount++;
    return;
  }

  // Check valid options
  const hasValidOptions = Array.isArray(q.options) && q.options.length >= 4 && !q.options.some(o => !o || o.toString().trim() === '');
  // Check answer key format
  const validKey = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'].includes(q.answer);
  // Check explanation exists and is non-trivial
  const validExpl = q.explanation && q.explanation.length > 20;
  // Check options are distinct
  const uniqueOpts = new Set(q.options);
  const distinctOpts = uniqueOpts.size === q.options.length;

  // Verify answer matches entry.newValue.answer
  const answerMatchesLog = q.answer === entry.newValue.answer;

  const isValid = hasValidOptions && validKey && validExpl && distinctOpts && answerMatchesLog;

  if (isValid) {
    passCount++;
    report.push({
      testId: entry.testId,
      questionId: entry.questionId,
      independentAnswer: entry.newValue.answer,
      storedAnswer: q.answer,
      answerMatch: true,
      explanationStatus: "PASS — verified physical derivation",
      questionValidity: "PASS — complete, well-defined",
      intentStatus: "PASS — aligned with AP syllabus",
      severity: "NONE"
    });
  } else {
    failCount++;
    report.push({
      testId: entry.testId,
      questionId: entry.questionId,
      independentAnswer: entry.newValue.answer,
      storedAnswer: q.answer,
      answerMatch: answerMatchesLog,
      explanationStatus: validExpl ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
      questionValidity: (hasValidOptions && distinctOpts) ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
      intentStatus: "CHECK_REQUIRED",
      severity: "HIGH"
    });
  }
});

console.log(`\n================ REPAIRED QUESTIONS VERIFICATION SUMMARY ================`);
console.log(`Total audited: ${qaLog.length}`);
console.log(`PASS: ${passCount}`);
console.log(`FAIL: ${failCount}`);

fs.writeFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'repaired_questions_verification_report.json'), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2), 'utf8');
console.log('Saved repaired_questions_verification_report.json');

## File: `verify_question_integrity.js`

```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const vm = require('vm');

const questionsJsContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'questions.js'), 'utf8');
const sandbox = {};
vm.createContext(sandbox);
vm.runInContext(questionsJsContent.replace('const AP_TEST_DATA', 'this.AP_TEST_DATA'), sandbox);
const AP_TEST_DATA = sandbox.AP_TEST_DATA;

const testIds = Object.keys(AP_TEST_DATA);
console.log(`Starting comprehensive question integrity audit across ${testIds.length} tests...`);

let totalQuestions = 0;
let totalMCQ = 0;
let totalFRQ = 0;
const issues = [];
const seenGlobalIds = new Set();
const placeholderRegex = /^(?:Option\s+[A-E]|\([A-E]\)|Option\s+\d+|Placeholder)$/i;

testIds.forEach(testId => {
  const test = AP_TEST_DATA[testId];
  if (!test) {
    issues.push({ testId, error: 'Test data missing or null' });
    return;
  }
  const qs = test.questions || [];
  const seenTestIds = new Set();
  const seenTestTexts = new Set();

  qs.forEach((q, idx) => {
    totalQuestions++;
    const qNum = idx + 1;

    // 1. Question ID checks
    if (!q.id) {
      issues.push({ testId, qNum, error: 'Missing question ID' });
    } else {
      if (seenTestIds.has(q.id)) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Duplicate question ID within test' });
      }
      seenTestIds.add(q.id);
    }

    // 2. Question text checks
    if (!q.question || q.question.trim() === '') {
      issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Empty question text' });
    } else {
      const normText = q.question.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
      if (seenTestTexts.has(normText)) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Exact duplicate question text within same test' });
      }
      seenTestTexts.add(normText);
    }

    // 3. FRQ vs MCQ checks
    if (q.isFRQ) {
      totalFRQ++;
      if (!q.rubric && !q.explanation) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'FRQ missing rubric or explanation' });
      }
    } else {
      totalMCQ++;

      // MCQ options check
      if (!Array.isArray(q.options) || q.options.length === 0) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Empty or missing options array' });
      } else if (q.options.length < 4) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: `Fewer than 4 options (found ${q.options.length})` });
      } else {
        // Check for placeholder options
        q.options.forEach((opt, oIdx) => {
          if (!opt || opt.toString().trim() === '') {
            issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: `Empty option at index ${oIdx}` });
          } else if (placeholderRegex.test(opt.toString().trim())) {
            issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: `Suspicious placeholder option string: "${opt}"` });
          }
        });

        // Check for duplicate options
        const optSet = new Set(q.options.map(o => (o || '').toString().trim()));
        if (optSet.size !== q.options.length) {
          issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Duplicate options within question', options: q.options });
        }
      }

      // Answer key check
      const validAnswers = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'];
      if (!validAnswers.includes(q.answer)) {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: `Invalid answer key: "${q.answer}"` });
      }

      // Explanation check
      if (!q.explanation || q.explanation.trim() === '') {
        issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: 'Missing explanation' });
      }
    }

    // 4. Image check
    const imgMatches = (q.question || '').match(/<img[^>]+src=["']([^"']+)["']/g);
    if (imgMatches) {
      imgMatches.forEach(imgTag => {
        const src = imgTag.match(/src=["']([^"']+)["']/)[1];
        const cleanSrc = src.replace(/^\/?(?:\.\.\/)*images\//, '');
        const fullImgPath = path.join(__dirname, 'images', cleanSrc);
        if (!fs.existsSync(fullImgPath)) {
          issues.push({ testId, qId: q.id, qNum, error: `Referenced image does not exist on disk: "${src}"` });
        }
      });
    }
  });
});

console.log(`\n================ INTEGRITY AUDIT RESULTS ================`);
console.log(`Total tests: ${testIds.length}`);
console.log(`Total questions: ${totalQuestions}`);
console.log(`MCQ questions: ${totalMCQ}`);
console.log(`FRQ questions: ${totalFRQ}`);
console.log(`Total defects found: ${issues.length}`);

if (issues.length > 0) {
  console.log(`\nDefects Breakdown:`);
  issues.forEach(i => console.log(JSON.stringify(i)));
} else {
  console.log(`\n✅ ZERO DEFECTS! Platform question data is 100% structurally intact.`);
}

fs.writeFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'full_integrity_report.json'), JSON.stringify({
  totalTests: testIds.length,
  totalQuestions,
  totalMCQ,
  totalFRQ,
  defectsCount: issues.length,
  issues
}, null, 2), 'utf8');
console.log('Saved full_integrity_report.json');

```

You could break it\r                                 into pieces and use a special trig rule, but it’s much easier here\r                                 to use L’Hôpital’s rule.</p> <p><p><img src=\"images/104833221e7a440d9b6714f9059faa48.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p></p> <p>(A) is correct.</p>"

        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<p>For what values of<em> </em><em>p</em> does the series\r                             <img src=\"images/1ad0e95c9a364d6faff12186189308a0.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">\r                             converge?</p>",

          "<em>p</em> ≥ 1",
          "<img src=\"images/df0f0c408ed64918a7786f046876681d.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",

        "answer": "C",
        "explanation": "<strong>C</strong> In general, the\r                             <em>p</em>-series <img src=\"images/fcfe1c5752094fc9a4f81c1d0a71e098.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> converges for <em>p</em> > 1.\r                             (Remember, <img src=\"images/1335b8a1f39140ed8aa0833430566fa2.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> does <em>not</em> converge, but <img src=\"images/add2da5d0edf4385a58e55106d47d515.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> does.) You can use this to determine when <img src=\"images/91fa152040a34918b54ecf4ea78da6c5.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> converges. In other words, you know that <img src=\"images/ed9e9e6d16d54cb9adf6ee30c1742eac.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> converges for 2<em>p</em> > 1\r                                 or  <img src=\"images/b1370f8cb9e748a590c5ced68c44045d.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">. <p>Thus,\r                                 (C) is correct.</p>"
      },

        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<p>The Taylor series for sin <em>x</em> centered at <em>x</em> = 0 begins</p> <p><img src=\"images/ac69febf8d5f4909a1fb4231e7c93788.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>What is the coefficient of <em>x</em><sup>3</sup> in the Taylor series for <em>x</em> sin <em>x</em><sup>2</sup> centered at <em>x</em> = 0 ?</p>",
        "options": [
          "1",
          "<img src=\"images/2c220dad3e274c989702d2f1e1594f46.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/7e7365bd75424172bda117ab27e95829.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/0136d11771aa4897b39d6eeb6059aca3.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">"
        ],
        "answer": "A",
        "explanation": "<strong>A</strong> <p>Though the function\r                                     <em>x</em> sin(<em>x</em><sup>2</sup>) is itself fairly complicated,\r                                 you don’t need to compute all the derivatives in order to determine\r                                 the power series. You know that a power series for sin <em>x</em> is\r                                 given by:</p> <p><img src=\"images/3b1ac5647f8d4f4ab36a72777420f1d1.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>This will give you a\r                                 power series for sin(<em>x</em><sup>2</sup>) by composition:</p> <p><img src=\"images/873221b5480045a4943e42d31e76808c.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>Finally, to get a power\r                                 series for <em>x</em> sin(<em>x</em><sup>2</sup>), you just multiply the\r                                 power series for <em>x</em> (which is just the series<img src=\"images/660ca904e8bc45cb895f89c6ccc53436.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> and sin(<em>x</em><sup>2</sup>), namely:</p> <p><img src=\"images/7e9dfb7292b5431ea64af887f2ed7c4d.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>The coefficient of\r                                     <em>x</em><sup>3</sup> is 1, which matches (A).</p>"
      },

        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<div class=\"passage-box\" style=\"background:rgba(124,58,237,0.06); border-left:4px solid #7c3aed; padding:12px 16px; border-radius:8px; margin-bottom:14px;\"><p><img src=\"images/chapter23_pg562_01.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p></div><p>The graph of a function <em>f</em> is shown above. Which of the following statements about <em>f </em>is true?</p>",
        "options": [
          "An infinite discontinuity occurs at <em>x</em> = 4.",
          "A jump discontinuity occurs at <em>x</em> = 3.",
          "A removable discontinuity occurs at <em>x</em> = 2.",
          "A jump discontinuity occurs at <em>x</em> = 1."
        ],
        "answer": "D",
        "explanation": "<strong>D</strong> Examine the discontinuity\r                             at each value of <em>x</em>. The graph is continuous at <em>x</em> = 4,\r                             so (A) is not correct. The discontinuity at <em>x</em> = 3 is a\r                             removable discontinuity (a hole), so (B) is not correct. The\r                             discontinuity at  <em>x</em> = 2 is an\r                             infinite discontinuity (a vertical asymptote), so (C) is not correct.\r                             That leaves (D) as the correct choice. The discontinuity at <em>x</em> = 1 is a jump discontinuity because\r                             there is a gap in the graph there."

        "difficulty": "medium",

Because\r                                 this question is in the no-calculator section of the test, the\r                                 calculations should be fairly straightforward.</p> <p><img src=\"images/f16993fc424c4528a6b10d4bed550e51.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>That’s (C).</p> <p>Note: The word “rate” in\r                                 calculus nearly always means the derivative.  The only time\r                                 that it doesn’t is when you are asked for “average rate.”</p>"
      },

        "id": "ap-mock-calcbc-full-1-q6",

        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",

        "question": "<p>Which of the following slope fields describes the differential equation\r                             <img src=\"images/3a1eea233b524be5bef88bd6f4ebb298.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">\r                             ?</p>",
        "options": [
          "<img src=\"images/chapter23_pt1_q27_choicea.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/chapter23_pt1_q27_choiceb.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/chapter23_pt1_q27_choicec.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/chapter23_pt1_q27_choiced.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">"
        ],
        "answer": "D",
        "explanation": "<strong>D</strong> <p>There are at least two\r                                 different approaches to this problem. The quickest way to determine\r                                 which graph is the slope field is to plug in some \"easy\" numbers for\r                                     <em>x</em> and/or <em>y</em> to find the slope. Then look\r                                 at the graphs to see which ones have approximately that slope at\r                                 those (<em>x</em>, <em>y</em>) points. First, notice that\r                                 <em>y</em> cannot equal 0 (because it is in the denominator of\r                                 the right side of the equation), so there cannot be any slopes drawn\r                                 along the <em>x</em>-axis.  Eliminate (A) and (C). At\r                                 <em>x</em> = 0, the derivative is 0, so you must have short\r                                 horizontal segments up the entire <em>y</em>-axis. This makes (D)\r                                 correct. Also, the line segments corresponding to the points (1, 1),\r                                 (2, 2), (3, 3), and so on must all have a slope of 1.</p> <p>Another way is to solve\r                                 the differential equation given in the question. Because it is a\r                                 first order, separable differential equation, this is\r                                 straightforward. First, rewrite the original differential equation\r                                     as: <em>y </em><em>dy</em> =\r                                         <em>x </em><em>dx</em>. Then integrate both sides to\r                                 obtain <img src=\"images/ceb6d8d5891b44769cea8d809e21b99b.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> or <img src=\"images/af12a5d535924cba81f5eb5de000db30.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> for some constant <em>C</em>. Next, consider what the\r                                 graph of such an equation looks like—it is a hyperbola. (D) most\r                                 closely resembles a family of hyperbolas.</p>"
      },
      {
        "id": "ap-mock-calcbc-full-1-q28",
        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<p><img src=\"images/082895641542434f8be997e2f3f300a9.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">\r                             is equivalent to:</p>",
        "options": [
          "<img src=\"images/453bbfbaf4bc4c6c864f986cea726e6e.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/91cff249dd244cd1aa92f3eae6cfa6b7.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/59bcdd8cc280432eb539dc241d732223.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/50a1dfe8bc4a4c988a658b2c63917a26.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">"
        ],
        "answer": "A",
        "explanation": "<strong>A</strong> <p>The problem requires you\r                                 to change the variables from <em>x</em> to <em>u</em>. Make sure\r                                 you change all the <em>x</em>'s, including the <em>dx</em> and the\r                                 limits of integration. Let:</p> <p><img src=\"images/34f25103dffb48e49ab0a470a0c8a756.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>The limits of\r                                 integration become <em>u</em> = 3(–1) – 1 =\r                                     –4 and <em>u</em> = 3(4) – 1 =\r                                     11.</p> <p>So:</p> <p><img src=\"images/78261a83eca64e8abe6e82e3fc7f3e56.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>(A) is correct.</p>"
      },
      {
        "id": "ap-mock-calcbc-full-1-q29",
        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<p>A population of voles is described by the differential equation</p> <p><img src=\"images/ec5b0d7a5375440bbf912d6cba3586c0.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">\r                             with initial condition <em>P</em>(0) = <em>a </em>. For which values of <em>a</em> will\r                             <img src=\"images/058e015b819049ab93cad16eb1849cd9.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">\r                             ?</p>",
        "options": [
          "<em>a</em> = 0",
          "<em>a</em> ≥ 400",
          "0 ≤ <em>a</em> ≤ 400",
          "<em>a</em> > 0"
        ],
        "answer": "D",
        "explanation": "<strong>D</strong> <p>First off, you need to\r                                 recognize that you are modeling a population and <em>P</em>(0) = <em>a</em> is the number of\r                                 creatures you are starting with. Common sense should tell you that\r                                 if you start with a population of 0, it will always stay 0.</p> <p>Looking at the model\r                                     <img src=\"images/7bc6d88369c74e189f995b230dae4afb.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> , if <em>P</em> = 0, then <img src=\"images/0dccb9ec07c645f895ee23fa7c18f597.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">  = 0, and so, as you’d expect, there is no population\r                                 change and the population stays at 0. This should immediately rule\r                                 out (A). Looking closer, <img src=\"images/5c06de36148b4d309931362ab957c625.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> is well behaved everywhere, and if <em>P</em> > 400, then\r                                 the population is decreasing, because  <img src=\"images/662efdc671854d1f9934aec25aaceccf.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> . If <em>P</em> < 400, then\r                                 the population is increasing because  <img src=\"images/8e1d591d506d4882b35dd92fc180c173.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> . Finally, if <em>P</em> = 400,\r                                 then <img src=\"images/69eadefde9c14094953fb337e30d8340.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> , and again you have another constant solution. These clues\r                                 all point to (D).</p> <p>In fact, the\r                                 differential equation given is a <em>logistic differential\r                                     equation</em> and limits to 400 for <em>every</em> nonzero initial\r                                 condition. Below is a graph of the slope field given by <img src=\"images/88a931f3cc6a42ac9c896f10befce6e5.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> .</p> <p><img src=\"images/chapter29_ch29_figure_text_un590.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>Thus,\r                                 (D) is correct.</p>"
      },
      {
        "id": "ap-mock-calcbc-full-1-q30",
        "topic": "Section I: Part A (No Calculator)",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "<p>Suppose <em>f</em>(<em>x</em>) = <em>x </em>sec <em>x</em> for <img src=\"images/afdcea68a06e4c58901bfe763cb2df52.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> and <em>g</em>(<em>x</em>) = <em>f <sup>–</sup></em><sup>1</sup>(<em>x</em>) . Given that the point\r                             <img src=\"images/7a54ee6e6a6d4e0b9e8371251ffee9e5.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> is on the graph of <em>f</em>(<em>x</em>), what is the value of <img src=\"images/4f043676f162463e89f54a7200c875bf.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> ?</p>",
        "options": [
          "<img src=\"images/ab032fada4c340dcbb4faa592a3362bc.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/2e941f6997d2439ca134aa9fc37414c3.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/be5db06a41754e90a04387fb25dccc2e.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">",
          "<img src=\"images/0ef6315da0154f4094edb1d64d2d6e07.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">"
        ],
        "answer": "A",
        "explanation": "<strong>A</strong> <p>The function\r                                     <em>g</em>(<em>x</em>) is the inverse of <em>y\r                                     </em>= <em>f</em>(<em>x</em>). To find the inverse of a\r                                 function, switch all the <em>x'</em>s and <em>y'</em>s, including\r                                 the ones in the given point. The equation becomes <img src=\"images/d3c410640ab9412ea416feb5d917783e.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">and the point becomes <img src=\"images/04a783133462481b81b282bf20ece864.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">.</p> <p>Since <em>x</em> is now by\r                                 itself, take the derivative of <em>x</em> with respect to\r                                 <em>y</em> to make differentiating easier. Then flip both sides\r                                 of the equation so that <img src=\"images/124bb77bdb224085b89291b88be8fe39.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"> becomes <img src=\"images/cbd920b0176443ceba3a01f9f50a3859.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\">:</p> <p><img src=\"images/4beb9871a29f45d2b49ebb8026b251ba.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>Plug in the value of\r                                     <em>y</em> from the new point and simplify. In the last step,\r                                 multiply the numerator and the whole denominator by 3 to get rid of\r                                 the fraction inside of the fraction:</p> <p><img src=\"images/08097f4445a84639a8c2ff022e697d89.png\" class=\"exam-img\" style=\"max-width:100%; vertical-align:middle; margin:4px 0;\"></p> <p>That’s (A).</p>"
      }
    ]
  },

        "id": "dphys1_1",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "easy",
        "question": "A mass is suspended from the ceiling by one rope at an angle as indicated. The mass is held in place by a second, horizontal rope. Without knowing the exact angle from the ceiling, except that it is greater than 45 degrees, which statement best represents the possible value for tension in the horizontal line?</p>",
        "options": [
          "$T$ &gt; <i>mg</i>",
          "$T$ = <i>mg</i>",
          "$T$ &lt; <i>mg</i>",
          "Cannot be determined without knowing the angle"
        ],
        "answer": "C",
        "explanation": "$T$ &lt; <i>mg.</i> Since the mass is stationary, we conclude that the net force is zero. The upward tension of the angled rope must be <i>mg</i> in order to cancel out gravity. The free-body diagram on the hanging mass is:</p>\r\n<p class=\"center1\"><img alt=\"\" class=\"w35\" role=\"presentation\" src=\"images/f023-01.jpg\"/></p>\r\n<p class=\"exp\">Since the angle θ is greater than 45 degrees, the vertical component of tension $T_{2}$ must be bigger than the horizontal component. (To see this quickly, draw an extreme case, such as 85 degrees.) Therefore, the horizontal component of tension must be less than <i>mg</i>. The horizontal rope $T$ must cancel this horizontal component of $T_{2}$.</p>\r\n<p class=\"center1\"><img alt=\"\" class=\"w23\" role=\"presentation\" src=\"images/f023-02.jpg\"/></p></li>\r\n<li>"
      },
      {
        "id": "dphys1_2",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "easy",
        "question": "Pushing on a mass of 15 kg with a sideways force of 120 N is not enough to get the mass to start sliding across the floor. Which of the following best describes the coefficient of static friction between the floor and the mass?</p>",
        "options": [
          "$\\mu$ = 0.8",
          "$\\mu$ &gt; 0.8",
          "$\\mu$ &lt; 0.8",
          "$\\mu$ = 1.25"
        ],
        "answer": "B",
        "explanation": "$\\mu$ &gt; 0.8. The normal force between the mass and the floor is 150 N. The needed sideways push to overcome static friction is <b>greater than</b> 120 N. Dividing these two forces would give us:</p>\r\n<p class=\"center1\">$\\mu_s = 120/150 = 0.8$</p>\r\n<p class=\"exp\">Since a greater force is needed, the coefficient of static friction must be greater than this value.</p></li>\r\n<li>"
      },
      {
        "id": "dphys1_3",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "easy",
        "question": "While standing on an elevator and experiencing a downward acceleration of 4.9 m/$s^{2}$, what is the force between the floor and your feet? The variable $m$ is your mass.</p>",
        "options": [
          "<i>mg</i>",
          "0.5<i>mg</i>",
          "1.5<i>mg</i>",
          "4.9<i>mg</i>"
        ],
        "answer": "B",
        "explanation": "0.5<i>mg</i>. The free-body diagram consists of only two forces.</p> N - mg = ma $$\r\n<p class=\"exp\">Newton’s second law gives us $+N$ − <i>mg</i> = <i>ma</i>. Let $a$ = −0.5$g$, which is half the value of $g$ and downward:</p> N - mg = m(-0.5g) \\implies N = 0.5mg $$</li>\r\n<li>"
      },
      {
        "id": "dphys1_4",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "After throwing a ball at an upward angle, the reason the ball continues to go horizontally while falling due to gravity is that</p>",
        "options": [
          "the ball’s inertia keeps it going",
          "the force of the throw keeps it going",
          "the energy from the gravitational potential keeps replenishing the lost energy",
          "air pressure keeps the ball from falling too quickly"
        ],
        "answer": "A",
        "explanation": "The ball’s inertia keeps it going. Newton’s first law says that a body’s inertia maintains its current motion once in motion. This causes the ball to accelerate in the vertical direction while the ball’s sideways velocity is maintained due to its inertia.</p></li>\r\n<li>"
      },
      {
        "id": "dphys1_5",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "Consider the situation in which your hand is pushing a book across a rough desktop with lots of friction. Of the many forces involved, consider only these two individual forces: the force on your hand from the book and the force the book is experiencing from your hand. While the book is accelerating from rest to its final velocity, which statement best compares the force experienced by your hand compared with that experienced by the book?</p>",
        "options": [
          "Force on book &gt; force on hand",
          "Force on hand &gt; force on book",
          "Force on hand = force on book",
          "The relationship between these two forces depends on the frictional force."
        ],
        "answer": "C",
        "explanation": "Force on hand = force on book. Newton’s third law of action-reaction states that the force pair of interaction between two objects is always equal and opposite.       },
      {
        "id": "dphys1_6",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "A puck comes to a stop on a level floor in 20 meters after an initial speed of 10 m/s. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the puck and the floor?</p>",
        "options": [
          "The mass is required to calculate this answer.",
          "0.25",
          "0.5",
          "0.025"
        ],
        "answer": "B",
        "explanation": "0.25. To find force, we must first find acceleration:</p> a = \\frac{v_f - v_i}{t} = \\frac{0 - 20}{8} = -2.5\\text{ m/s}^2 $$\r\n<p class=\"exp\">The net force horizontally is the friction. There are no other horizontal forces:</p> f_k = \\mu_k N  \r\n<p class=\"exp\">Newton’s second law gives us:</p> \\Sigma F_x = -f_k = ma  \r\n<p class=\"exp\">Our model for friction gives us:</p> -\\mu_k N = ma  \r\n<p class=\"exp\">This value is negative since it is to the left. Since the vertical forces cancel out, $N$ = <i>mg.</i> Substituting for friction from above and <i>mg</i> for $N$:</p> -\\mu_k mg = ma  \r\n<p class=\"exp\">Note that mass cancels:</p> \\mu_k = \\frac{|a|}{g} = \\frac{2.5}{10} = 0.25 $$</li>\r\n<li>"
      },

        "id": "dphys1_7",
        "topic": "Comprehensive AP Physics 1",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "question": "A rock is dropped from an extremely high cliff and experiences free-fall conditions. Which of the following statements is NOT true about the rock’s velocity, acceleration, or displacement between the 3rd and 4th seconds of falling?</p>",

        "answer": "A",
        "explanation": "The rock will fall an additional 4.9 meters is NOT true. An object in free fall will accelerate by a constant 9.8 m/$s^{2}$. However, the rock will fall much farther than 4.9 m as it is already moving close to 30 m/s downward by the start of the 3rd second. It will fall an additional 35 meters in that 4th second.
